name: Hyundai i30 N TCR
hook: The man who drove the very first test laps of Hyundai's first circuit racer went on to win a world title in it, at 56.
story:
In September 2016, Hyundai had never built a car purely for circuit racing. So it called Gabriele Tarquini.

He was an Italian with more than twenty years in front-wheel-drive touring cars. He had won titles in Britain, in Europe and in the world series. Now he would be the test driver for a brand-new racer.

In April 2017, the i30 N TCR turned its first laps at Motorland Aragón in Spain, with Tarquini at the wheel. That October, he and Alain Menu raced it in China. The first customer cars went out in December.

Then came 2018, and a new world cup for cars like this one. Tarquini won its very first race, in Morocco. He won five races that year.

It all came down to Macau, the tight street track by the sea. He finished tenth in the last race. It was enough. He took the title by three points from Yvan Muller.

Tarquini was 56. That made him the oldest world champion in FIA history. The car he helped shape had carried him there.
description: The i30 N TCR is a front-wheel-drive touring car built by Hyundai Motorsport in Alzenau, Germany, to the global TCR rules. It was Hyundai's first car designed purely for circuit racing. Based on the i30 five-door hatchback, it uses a 2.0-litre turbocharged Theta II four-cylinder making 350 hp, with a six-speed Xtrac sequential gearbox and paddle shift. Sold to customer teams from December 2017, it won both the drivers' and teams' titles in the 2018 World Touring Car Cup.
